01 — Example

Full, annotated implementation. Open this after a real attempt — ideally after kata submit 01 passes, then compare. Reading it first turns the exercise into copy-typing.

The complete compilable file is reference/ch01/agent/provider_openai.go. This document is that file taken apart, in the order the thinking happens.

The shape, before the code

Four jobs, four functions. Knowing the split matters more than the code:

Chat
 ├── buildRequest   Request  →  *http.Request     (translate our types → wire)
 ├── do            send, check status, or fail    (transport + error policy)
 └── fold           io.Reader → Message, Usage    (the delta log → one value)

If you write Chat as one 90-line function you will pass, and you will hate it in chapter 02 when the fold grows tool calls. Written as three functions, chapter 02 adds ~15 lines and touches nothing else.

Step 1 — translate, don't leak

Your Message and the wire's message are similar but not the same. Keep a wire type and a conversion function; never put json: tags on your domain types.

// Why a separate type: the wire has `tool_calls` as a nested object, ours has
// ToolCalls as a flat slice. When those diverge in chapter 02, only this file
// changes.
type wireRequest struct {
	Model       string        `json:"model"`
	Messages    []wireMessage `json:"messages"`
	Stream      bool          `json:"stream"`
	MaxTokens   *int          `json:"max_tokens,omitempty"`
	Temperature *float64      `json:"temperature,omitempty"`
	Tools       []wireTool    `json:"tools,omitempty"`
}

func toWireMessages(msgs []Message) []wireMessage { /* role + content */ }

Two details that are cheap now and expensive later:

  • *int / *float64 for optionals. With int, zero means both "unset" and

"zero", and you will one day send max_tokens: 0.

  • The model falls back: req.Model first, then p.Model. Chapter 05 sends

requests with no model when it reuses a session's provider.

Step 2 — the request, and the three things that are graded

url := strings.TrimRight(p.BaseURL, "/") + "/chat/completions"
httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, url, bytes.NewReader(body))
if err != nil {
	return Message{}, Usage{}, fmt.Errorf("build request: %w", err)
}
httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
httpReq.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
if p.APIKey != "" {
	httpReq.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+p.APIKey)
}
  • TrimRight(base, "/") so both http://x/v1 and http://x/v1/ work. Half the

"why is it 404" reports in the world are this.

  • NewRequestWithContext, not NewRequest. This is the only place ctx enters,

and it is what makes request-timeout pass.

  • stream: true in the body is required by the case, even though our

function returns a whole message. We stream because chapter 06 will want incremental events, and because learning the stream is the chapter.

Step 3 — fail the way a caller can act on

resp, err := client.Do(httpReq)
if err != nil {
	return Message{}, Usage{}, err   // already wraps ctx.Err() when cancelled
}
defer resp.Body.Close()

if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
	snippet, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4096))
	return Message{}, Usage{}, &HTTPError{Status: resp.StatusCode, Body: string(snippet)}
}

Three decisions worth defending:

  • Return client.Do's error unchanged. It already wraps context.Canceled;

wrapping it in a string would break errors.Is and fail request-timeout.

  • LimitReader, 4 KiB. Error pages are sometimes megabytes of HTML. You want

a diagnostic, not a memory event.

  • A typed error, not fmt.Errorf. *HTTPError is what lets the loop in

chapter 04 distinguish "retry with backoff" from "the model is wrong".

Step 4 — fold the stream

This is the chapter. Everything above is plumbing.

func readSSE(r io.Reader) (Message, Usage, error) {
	var (
		content strings.Builder
		usage   Usage
		calls   = map[int]*callAccumulator{}   // chapter 02; unused here
	)

	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), 4*1024*1024)

	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := scanner.Text()

		// SSE framing: blank separators, comments, and named fields other than data.
		if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, ":") || !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
			continue
		}

		data := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "data:"))
		if data == "" || data == "[DONE]" {
			continue
		}

		var chunk wireChunk
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &chunk); err != nil {
			return Message{}, Usage{}, fmt.Errorf("decode stream chunk: %w", err)
		}

		if chunk.Usage != nil {          // ← arrives once, on the last chunk
			usage = Usage{ /* ... */ }
		}
		for _, choice := range chunk.Choices {
			content.WriteString(choice.Delta.Content)   // ← append, never assign
			// tool_calls folding lives here from chapter 02
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {              // ← the 3rd trap
		return Message{}, Usage{}, fmt.Errorf("read stream: %w", err)
	}

	return Message{Role: RoleAssistant, Content: content.String()}, usage, nil
}

The chunk struct it decodes into, with the nesting that trips people up:

type wireChunk struct {
	Choices []struct {
		Delta struct {
			Content string `json:"content"`
		} `json:"delta"`
		FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason"`
	} `json:"choices"`
	Usage *struct {
		PromptTokens     int `json:"prompt_tokens"`
		CompletionTokens int `json:"completion_tokens"`
		TotalTokens      int `json:"total_tokens"`
	} `json:"usage"`
}

A top-level Delta field compiles, decodes without error, and produces an empty string for every chunk. That is the failure the case prints-reply reports as actual: "\n".

Why scanner.Buffer is not optional

bufio.Scanner has a 64 KiB default line limit. A chunk carrying a large tool result argument, or a provider that batches aggressively, will exceed it. When it does, Scan returns false and the only signal is scanner.Err() returning bufio.ErrTooLong. You will see: a truncated answer, no error, no clue.

Raising the cap to 4 MiB is a guess; every harness guesses. Production code (pi included) either raises it or replaces Scanner with a Reader-based framing loop that has no per-line ceiling. We raise it, and note the tradeoff.

Why [DONE] must be checked before unmarshalling

It is not JSON. json.Unmarshal on [DONE] returns invalid character 'D' looking for beginning of value, which the naive implementation wraps as "decode stream chunk" and reports as a protocol error — on a completely healthy stream. This is the single most common first-run failure in this chapter.

Step 5 — assemble outside the loop

msg := Message{Role: RoleAssistant, Content: content.String()}
return msg, usage, nil

Banal, but note where it happens: outside. Implementations that build the Message inside the loop and return it early end up with a message that has only the last delta. The loop's job is to mutate accumulators; the return's job is to snapshot them once.

The four diffs

Each of these is a real failure mode with a graded case. Left is what a competent first implementation does; right is the fix.

1. Assign instead of append — prints-reply

- msg.Content = choice.Delta.Content
+ content.WriteString(choice.Delta.Content)

2. Ignore the scanner's error — truncated-stream

  for scanner.Scan() { ... }
+ if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
+     return Message{}, Usage{}, err
+ }
  return Message{Content: content.String()}, usage, nil

3. Only decode chunks with content — debug-usage

- if choice.Delta.Content == "" { continue }
  if chunk.Usage != nil { usage = ... }

4. Background context — request-timeout

- http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, url, body)
+ http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, url, body)

That is the whole chapter: one fold, one error policy, one lifetime. The other two cases (request-shape, http-error) are structural and you either have them or your first run tells you immediately.

What production adds, and why we don't

FeatureFile in piWhy it is out of scope here
Retry with backoff + Retry-Afterapi/openai-completions.tschapter 04 gives you one retry path; a full policy is a chapter of its own
Prompt caching headersapi/openai-prompt-cache.tsprovider-specific, no teaching value
~30 provider wire formatsproviders/*.tsone adapter teaches the abstraction; thirty teach maintenance
Abort mid-tool-callagent/agent-loop.tschapter 08
Token counting before sendagent/context_tokens.go (PiG)chapter 07

The one thing worth stealing early, when you get to chapter 07: pi estimates tokens before sending, so it can refuse a request rather than discover the overflow from a 400. That is a design decision, not a feature, and it is easier to add while Chat is still small.

Comparison checklist

When you look at reference/ch01, check whether yours differs in:

  • [ ] separate wire types vs json tags on domain types
  • [ ] *int for optionals
  • [ ] client.Do error returned unwrapped
  • [ ] typed *HTTPError
  • [ ] scanner.Buffer raised
  • [ ] [DONE] handled before Unmarshal
  • [ ] scanner.Err() checked
  • [ ] message assembled outside the loop

Differences outside this list are style. Differences inside it are bugs waiting for a later chapter.
